details.label: Discussion
details.text: Aided by forcing for ascent ahead of a mid-level perturbation and along/ahead of a surface stationary/cold front, scattered thunderstorm development is expected along the Front Range from southeastern Wyoming into northern Colorado over the next 1-2 hours. Storms will be initially high-based given hot temperatures and well-mixed boundary layer profiles (low-90s F temperatures amid dewpoints in the mid-40s) ahead of the aforementioned surface boundary. While effective shear around 35-40 kts will be sufficient for supercell structures, high cloud bases (LCLs of 2+ km AGL) and steep low-level lapse rates will favor efficient evaporative cooling, downdraft formation, and upscale growth/clustering as convection evolves eastward. Severe wind gusts (a few significant) will be the main threat with this activity, but large to very large hail is also expected, especially early in the convective cycle and with any convection that is able to maintain a discrete mode. A Severe Thunderstorm Watch will likely be needed for at least a portion of the discussion area in the next 1-2 hours to cover these threats

details.label: Most probable threats
details.text: MOST PROBABLE PEAK WIND GUST...65-80 MPH · MOST PROBABLE PEAK HAIL SIZE...1.50-2.50 IN

details.label: Summary
details.text: Isolated severe storms capable of marginally severe hail and/or damaging wind gusts appear possible late this afternoon. A watch is not currently expected due to the limited areal coverage of the severe weather threat

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Recent visible satellite imagery shows areas of deepening cumulus within a broadly confluent zone stretching through central lower MI, from KLDM to KD95. While multilevel clouds have slowed diabatic heating and resultant air mass destabilization, modification of the 15Z DTX sounding for current surface conditions yields MLCAPE of 1000-1500 J/kg. Water vapor imagery suggests that stronger forcing for ascent associated with a weak mid-level disturbance is currently shifting to the east of the region with low-level convergence and modest warm advection serving as the primary sources for widely scattered storm development by late afternoon. Additionally, surface observations and visible satellite suggest convective outflow from ongoing storms over IN and OH surging north, which may also focus storm development. Regional VWPs are sampling 40-50+ kt west-northwest winds generally above 4 km AGL, which are yielding sufficient deep-layer shear for some storm organization, including episodic supercell structures. Poor mid-level lapse rates of less than 7 C/km should limit hail sizes, though some marginally severe hail appears possible with the strongest storms. Damaging wind potential will be contingent on storms merging into clusters, leading to some cold pool organization

details.label: Most probable threats
details.text: MOST PROBABLE PEAK WIND GUST...UP TO 60 MPH · MOST PROBABLE PEAK HAIL SIZE...UP TO 1.25 IN

details.label: Summary
details.text: Scattered thunderstorms will develop eastward into the Black Hills/western South Dakota vicinity through this afternoon, bringing a threat for large to very large hail and severe wind gusts

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Latest radar imagery depicts a developing supercell in close proximity to a surface low across northeastern Wyoming. Aided by weak ascent ahead of a mid-level perturbation and easterly, upslope flow (surface dewpoints ranging from the low 60s F to near 70 farther east), convection will expand in coverage through the afternoon as it evolves eastward into the Black Hills/western South Dakota vicinity. While the 18z UNR observed sounding depicted lingering inhibition, filtered diurnal heating should gradually reduce inhibition through the afternoon. For ongoing/developing convection, steep mid-level lapse rates (8+ C/km), 40-50+ kts of effective shear, and relatively straight, elongated hodographs will support supercells as the initial storm mode, with large to very large hail the primary hazard. Increasing storm coverage lends uncertainty to how long discrete supercells will be maintained, with eventual upscale growth/cluster development expected to yield a transition towards severe wind gusts as the primary hazard. Should a discrete mode be maintained for longer, however, very large hail to 3 inches in diameter would be possible. A Severe Thunderstorm Watch will likely be needed for a portion of the area within the hour

details.label: Most probable threats
details.text: MOST PROBABLE PEAK WIND GUST...65-80 MPH · MOST PROBABLE PEAK HAIL SIZE...2.00-3.50 IN
